candidate.answerReason: The nine outer bases and the horizontal bottom segment form a ten-sided polygon. Its angles give 18a=1440 degrees, so the outer-base angle is 80 degrees and the larger trapezoid angle is 100 degrees.

methods.label: Count the angles of the outer polygon
methods.explanation:
Close the outer rim by joining its two bottom endpoints along the horizontal line. The nine outer bases and this bottom segment form a ten-sided polygon, allowing us to use its angle sum.

Let \(a\) be an interior angle at an outer base of a trapezoid. The two angles at that base are equal because the trapezoid is isosceles: dropping perpendiculars from the shorter base to the longer base produces two right triangles with equal hypotenuses and equal heights, so they are congruent. Congruence of the nine trapezoids makes this same angle \(a\) occur throughout the outer rim.

At each of the eight junctions between consecutive outer bases, the polygon's interior angle is the sum of two trapezoid angles, or \(2a\). At each of the two bottom corners, its angle is \(a\). These account for all ten vertices. Therefore
\[
8(2a)+2a=(10-2)180^\circ,
\]
so
\[
18a=1440^\circ,
\qquad a=80^\circ.
\]
The angles along a leg of a trapezoid are supplementary because its bases are parallel. Thus the other angle is \(180^\circ-80^\circ=100^\circ\), which is the larger one. Hence \(\boxed{x=100^\circ}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses elementary congruence, parallel-line angle relationships, and the interior-angle sum of a polygon.

methods.label: Divide the half-turn among the trapezoids
methods.explanation:
Track the directions of the nonparallel sides, always pointing from the outside of the arch toward its opening. The leftmost side points horizontally right, and the rightmost side points horizontally left. Moving across the arch as shown, these directions make a total clockwise turn of \(180^\circ\).

Let \(a\) be an angle at an outer base. The two angles there are equal: perpendiculars from the shorter base to the longer base give two right triangles with equal leg hypotenuses and equal heights, so they are congruent.

Extend the two legs of one trapezoid toward the opening until they meet. The resulting triangle has base angles \(a\) and \(a\), so its vertex angle is
\[
\theta=180^\circ-2a.
\]
Reversing both rays of an angle preserves its measure, so this is also the change between the two inward-pointing leg directions. The congruent trapezoids contribute equal changes, and there is one change for each of the nine trapezoids. Consequently,
\[
9\theta=180^\circ,
\qquad \theta=20^\circ.
\]
It follows that \(a=(180^\circ-20^\circ)/2=80^\circ\). Parallel bases make adjacent angles along a leg supplementary, so the larger trapezoid angle is
\[
\boxed{x=180^\circ-80^\circ=100^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: This route uses only triangle angle sums and the interpretation of an angle as a turn. It does not require assuming that all extended legs meet at one point.
